note: Permanent memory of QA-SYSTEM failures (controls that could produce false confidence), each bound to the detector that now closes it. QA_CONTROL_ESCAPES_OPEN must be 0 before QA_SYSTEM_READY. A reintroduced control escape must make its detector fail — proven by src/engineering-os/qaControlEscapeCorpus.test.ts.

escapes.originalFailure: qa-monster.mjs exited `pass ? 0 : 1` (area roll-up), so RC exited 0 while QA_SYSTEM=INCOMPLETE_PRODUCTIZATION.
escapes.howFalseConfidence: CI wiring the command would go green on a non-ready system.

escapes.originalFailure: A certification report could be edited after the fact with no detection.
A hash-consistent capsule could omit a required claim (or a new required claim could be added after sealing).
escapes.howFalseConfidence: An internally-consistent capsule would appear complete while covering less than the denominator.

escapes.originalFailure: A required RC area could be silently absent from the report and still exit 0.
escapes.howFalseConfidence: Fewer areas evaluated would read as full coverage.

escapes.originalFailure: HEAD (harness) was conflated with the deployed runtime source SHA.
escapes.howFalseConfidence: A harness-only commit would appear to change the certified runtime.

escapes.originalFailure: After a runtime change, an old artifact could still be treated as the current candidate.
MACHINE_CLOSABLE_REMAINING came from a hand-written list, so an obligation could be silently dropped.
escapes.howFalseConfidence: Dropping an obligation would falsely read as 0 remaining.

escapes.originalFailure: The stochastic sampling universe was hand-written, so a model-dependent claim could be omitted from sampling.
escapes.howFalseConfidence: An unsampled model-exposed claim would appear covered.

escapes.originalFailure: The deployed-secret scanner could scan a hidden default target instead of the candidate.
escapes.howFalseConfidence: A clean unrelated target would certify a dirty candidate.

escapes.originalFailure: Per-instance in-memory rate limiting could be described as a global/distributed limit.
escapes.howFalseConfidence: Abuse protection would appear stronger than it is.

escapes.originalFailure: A yield/handoff could occur while machine-closable work remained, justified only by 'large program' / 'practical context'.
escapes.howFalseConfidence: Incomplete productization would look like a legitimate stopping point.
